clue.text: Bishop comes to unusual Serbian city

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the next word are put in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A bishop pays a visit to some strange Serbian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the state capital of Queensland in Australia, an example of a city.

clue.text: Ornament Edward found in stream

indicators.note: found in means the name sits inside the stream

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a stream
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: An ornament belonging to Edward turns up in a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to decorate or adorn, the verb sense of ornament.

clue.text: Imprisoned at home, expressed grief audibly

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: audibly signals we want a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: sighed means let out a sad breath

explanation.surface: A person confined indoors sighed in sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is informal slang for in prison, so it equals imprisoned.

clue.text: Be joining skipper finally on ship — a German

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word skipper

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German joins the crew, the captain at last on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is someone from Berlin, so is a German.

clue.text: Pleasant member of family becoming heartless

indicators.note: becoming heartless means the central letter of the relative is dropped

parts.note: a niece is a relative, a sibling's daughter

explanation.surface: A pleasant relative turns cold and unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are synonyms for agreeable.

clue.text: Sealing device for cleaner

definitions.meaning: a small flat ring fitted under a nut or tap to make a seal
one who cleans, as a dishwasher or window cleaner does

explanation.surface: A plumber's part goes by another name for someone who cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a flat sealing ring in plumbing and any person or machine that washes things.

clue.text: More than one saw notice over long period

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the notice sits above the long period

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone spotted something more than once over a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb, so several of them are adages.

clue.text: General as one who would eat human flesh hot not cold!

indicators.note: hot not cold means the letter for cold is swapped for the letter for hot, as on taps

parts.words: one who would eat human flesh
parts.note: a cannibal eats the flesh of its own kind

explanation.surface: A military commander described as a man-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: H and C are the hot and cold marks on British taps. The name also nods to Hannibal Lecter, the fictional cannibal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal was the Carthaginian general who crossed the Alps with elephants.

clue.text: Those left, having ignored a prompt

indicators.note: having ignored means the following letter is dropped from the leftovers

parts.note: the remainder is what is left over

explanation.surface: People who stayed behind ignored a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is something that jogs the memory, which is a prompt.

clue.text: Grade C is terrible shame

indicators.note: terrible here signals the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolchild laments that getting a mere C grade is a shameful result.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' belongs to the fodder rather than being a link word, so all eight letters of 'Grade C is' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace and shame are synonyms for loss of honour or standing.

clue.text: Pub with group of miners who provided fair entertainment?

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' trade union

explanation.surface: Miners gathering in a pub, wondering who supplied the fairground fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM was the British miners' union, famous for the 1984-85 strike.
explanation.definitionFit: P. T. Barnum was the American showman and circus founder, so his entertainment was of the travelling-fair kind.

clue.text: Agent having imbibed drink, upset, bad-tempered

indicators.note: having imbibed means the agent swallows the drink, holding it inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the drink is turned upside down

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A spy who has had too much to drink becomes upset and irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like part of the agent's mood, but in a down clue it turns the drink upside down before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for argumentative and sulky, so bad-tempered.

clue.text: Fellow attached to many different clubs

definitions.text: Fellow attached to many different clubs

parts.words: Fellow attached to many different clubs
parts.note: sounds like a social man who joins lots of societies, but the clubs are golf clubs, carried round the course by an assistant

explanation.surface: A sociable man belongs to numerous clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's assistant carries a whole bag of different clubs, so is literally attached to them.

clue.text: City resident presenting three articles about province

indicators.note: about means the three articles are placed around the next piece

parts.note: the articles A, THE and AN together
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A city dweller writes three pieces about a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' looks like newspaper pieces, but means the grammatical articles. Northern Ireland is known in the UK simply as 'the Province'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in Athens, a Greek city, is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Sailor on a steamship, incompetent fool

parts.note: Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor on a steamer proves to be a clumsy idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a male donkey, used figuratively for a stupid person.

clue.text: The French and British soon to meet in the country

parts.note: le is French for the
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: French and British diplomats are about to have a meeting abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a nation on the eastern Mediterranean, an example of a country.

clue.text: Mist with tree not totally visible

indicators.note: not totally means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: the hazel is a small nut-bearing tree

explanation.surface: A tree is half hidden in a mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Haze is a thin mist or fog, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Stocky England batsman once in tricky test

indicators.note: in means the batsman goes inside the rearranged letters
tricky means the letters of test are twisted around

parts.note: Graeme Hick batted for England in Test cricket in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A sturdy former England cricketer in a difficult Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges 'test' to TSET before the batsman, Graeme Hick, goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means heavily built and broad, the same as stocky.

clue.text: Huge quantity swirling in a tum, no?

indicators.note: swirling means the letters churn into a new order

explanation.surface: Is that a large amount churning in your belly, or not?
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain is used informally for a great heap of something, as in a mountain of paperwork.

clue.text: Vet, I will struggle with an ox creating bother

indicators.note: struggle means these letters wrestle themselves into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A vet admits a fight with an ox will cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation is annoyance or irritation, the sense of bother as a noun.

clue.text: Criminal who robbed the rich?

definitions.meaning: slang for a gangster or thug
Robin ..., the outlaw of English legend who stole from the rich to give to the poor

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a gangster and the surname of the legendary Sherwood Forest outlaw.

clue.text: Butterfly — something flying up, keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a skier, also spelt skyer, is a cricket ball hit high into the air
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A butterfly flutters upward silently.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a skier (or skyer) is a ball struck steeply upward, often an easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Skippers are a family of small, darting butterflies, so this is an example of the insect.

clue.text: Seabird spotted in wonderful Margate

indicators.note: spotted in means the answer can be seen tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A seabird is sighted at the lovely seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white petrel of the North Atlantic, an example of a seabird.

clue.text: Boss dismissing men is not mincing words

indicators.note: dismissing means the men are sacked from the boss's title

parts.note: a director is a boss of a company
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A manager sacks staff and speaks bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being direct is speaking frankly and plainly, which is not softening one's language.

clue.text: Big meals, fine food, with seconds devoured

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: devoured means seconds are swallowed inside the food

parts.note: eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Large dinners of good food, with second helpings polished off.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts are lavish banquets, so they are large meals.

clue.text: After study look for mastery

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
to quest is to search or look for

explanation.surface: Having studied, someone hunts for expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a victory over something, which gives mastery of it.

clue.text: Spite shown by nasty little creatures following mum

indicators.note: following means the creatures are placed after mum

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
lice are small unpleasant parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Mum is followed around by horrid little bugs and shows ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice and spite are synonyms for the wish to harm someone.

clue.text: Christmas visitors marvellous? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: magic is informal for wonderful or marvellous

explanation.surface: Were the Christmas guests wonderful? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men from the East who visited the infant Jesus, part of the Nativity story.

clue.text: Obsequious host following modern miss around

indicators.note: following means the host comes after the title
around means the title is turned back to front

parts.note: Ms is the modern title for a woman, replacing Miss
a host is a great crowd or army

explanation.surface: A fawning host trails after a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like someone entertaining guests, but means an army, as in the heavenly host.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes an oily, ingratiating manner, which is what obsequious means.

clue.text: Circumspection of one head backing conflict

indicators.note: backing means one and head stand behind the conflict

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: A cautious leader supports a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness means caution, and circumspection is careful consideration before acting.

clue.text: Some monument undraped and plain

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A statue has been unveiled and is unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'and plain' included the link word 'and'; the definition is 'plain' alone, a noun here though it looks like the adjective meaning unadorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain, so the answer is a type of plain.

clue.text: Receiver of holy letter about hostelry gets unpleasant sensation

indicators.note: about means the receiver's name goes around the hostelry

parts.note: Titus received Paul's Epistle to Titus in the New Testament
an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: Someone sent a sacred letter at a pub ends up feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is a ringing or buzzing in the ears, a distressing bodily sensation.
